extra.message: Username and password from the login form (routes/login.js req.body) are concatenated directly into a SQL query string executed via pg-promise's db.one(). An attacker can log in as any user or dump data using payloads like username=' OR '1'='1'-- .
product_id comes unsanitized from the query string (routes/products.js '/products/detail?id=') and is concatenated directly into a SQL query, allowing SQL injection.
The search query parameter 'q' (routes/products.js '/products/search') is concatenated directly into a SQL ILIKE query without escaping, allowing SQL injection.

All fields of the purchase cart (mail, product_name, address, ship_date, phone, price — all taken directly from user request body/query in routes/products.js '/products/buy') are concatenated into an INSERT statement without parameterization, allowing SQL injection.

username, sourced from req.session.user_name which is set directly from the unsanitized login form username (routes/login.js line 30), is concatenated into a SQL query, allowing SQL injection via the login username field that later executes here.

check_logged() only calls res.redirect() when the session is not logged in but never calls return/next() to halt execution, and does not signal the caller to stop. Every route in routes/products.js calls check_logged(req, res) without checking a return value or returning afterward, so the protected handler logic (DB query and res.render of product/purchase data) still executes for unauthenticated users regardless of the redirect, constituting a broken access-control check.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: check_logged(req, res) is called without 'return' and without checking its result; execution continues to db_products.list() and res.render() even when the user is not authenticated, exposing product data to unauthenticated requests (same pattern repeated at lines 26, 43, 64, 91).

After successful authentication, res.redirect(returnurl) redirects to a URL taken directly from req.body.returnurl with no validation that it is a local/relative path. An attacker can craft a login link with returnurl=http://evil.com to redirect victims to an attacker-controlled site after login.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The 'returnurl' query parameter (routes/login.js url_params.returnurl) is rendered with EJS's unescaped output tag <%- %> into an HTML attribute value, allowing reflected XSS, e.g. returnurl="><script>alert(1)</script>.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: auth_error (the 'error' query parameter, populated from err.message in routes/login.js's failed-auth catch handler) is rendered unescaped via <%- %>, allowing reflected XSS through the login error message, e.g. /login?error=<script>alert(1)</script>.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The search query 'q' (routes/products.js '/products/search', url_params.q) is echoed back with EJS's unescaped output tag <%- %>, allowing reflected XSS, e.g. /products/search?q=<script>alert(1)</script>.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Purchase fields (product_name, mail, phone, ship_date, address) are taken unsanitized from the '/products/buy' request in routes/products.js, stored via model/products.js purchase(), and later rendered here with unescaped <%- %> tags. An attacker can submit a malicious script as e.g. product_name or address during checkout, which then executes in the browser of anyone (the same user, or an admin/support viewer) viewing the purchased-products page — stored XSS.

extra.message: PostgreSQL connection strings with hardcoded username and password ('postgres:postgres') are committed in source for local, devel, and docker configs (also lines 12 and 20).
The express-session 'secret' used to sign session cookies is a hardcoded string literal in source control. Anyone with access to the repo can forge valid session cookies.
Session cookie is configured with secure: false (sent over plain HTTP, vulnerable to interception) and an effectively unlimited maxAge (99999999999 ms, ~3170 years), preventing session expiry.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: When app.get('env') === 'development' (the default when NODE_ENV is unset), the full error object including stack trace is passed to the 'error' view, which renders it directly to the client (see views/error.ejs line 3), leaking internal implementation details such as file paths and query fragments.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: On failed login, the raw database error message (err.message, from pg-promise/PostgreSQL) is appended to the redirect URL and later rendered on the login page, potentially exposing SQL query fragments or database internals to the attacker.
